facility_roles.note: SNOLAB is the planned site, not yet an installed one: the nEXO site says the experiment 'will be built in SNOLAB' (future tense), and no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) says the detector has been installed there.
facility_roles.quote: the experiment will be built in SNOLAB, a deep mine. At two kilometers down, the rock overburden protects the entire experiment from cosmic radiation that is too energetic to be stopped by artificial shields.

intervals.label: design and construction preparation
intervals.note: No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives a start date for this phase or confirms that the detector itself is physically under construction; the collaboration describes itself as contributing to 'design and construction' of the eventual detector. A secondary summary describes an anticipated construction start around 2026 and commissioning around 2032-2033; that was not found in any primary source consulted, so it is not recorded as a dated interval. Status is recorded as `proposed` rather than `construction` pending a clearer sourced statement. `start` (2018) is the date of the earliest dated nEXO design document found (the Pre-Conceptual Design Report), a lower bound on the design and preparation phase, not a true construction-start date.
intervals.quote: A consortium of over 150 scientists and technologists from 31 institutions and eight countries are contributing to the design and construction of nEXO.

intervals.label: US-led project paused (listed by SNOLAB, December 2024)
intervals.note: Recorded as an annotation (kind phase) with status `proposed`. SNOLAB Report, slides dated 26 May 2026, slide 26 'SNOLAB Cryopit Timeline': the first entry, dated 'Dec 2024', says "US led nEXO project was paused."; the next entries are XLZD approved as a conceptual design study at SNOLAB (August 2025) and Canadian scientists joining the XLZD collaboration (March 2026). The nEXO website (nexo.llnl.gov, undated; read again 2026-10-25) still says "The nEXO experiment is under development", and SNOLAB's 31 July 2026 talk lists 'nEXO 2.0' among illustrative future-project ideas that 'does not indicate SNOLAB approval or space allocation'. No source says the project was cancelled, so it is not recorded as `cancelled`. The date is the one printed on the SNOLAB slide; no source consulted gives the pause's own announcement.
intervals.quote: US led nEXO project was paused.

quantity.quote: nEXO will search for neutrinoless double beta decay in 5,000 kg of the xenon-136 (136Xe) isotope ... so we use xenon that is enriched to 90% in that isotope

name: nEXO
notes: Planned for the SNOLAB underground laboratory (facility:snolab, site:snolab-underground-lab).

Status is recorded as 'proposed': no source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) confirms that physical construction has begun, and the nEXO site (nexo.llnl.gov, undated) says 'The nEXO experiment is under development.' A secondary web summary described a phased 'nEXO 2.0' plan (construction start ~2026, commissioning ~2032-2033); it was not found in any primary source consulted and is not recorded as a sourced value.
No INSPIRE experiment-registry identifier is recorded for nEXO (external.inspire_experiment is empty).
No source consulted (checked 2026-10-25) gives the collaboration's formation date.

physics_goals.note: A Majorana neutrino is one that is its own antiparticle: pCDR Sec. 2 describes the Majorana mass term as associated with fermions "for which the antiparticle state coincides with the particle state".
physics_goals.quote: nEXO is a tonne-scale neutrinoless double beta (0νββ) decay search in 136Xe ... its observation would confirm the existence of Majorana neutrinos, regardless of the decay mechanism
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 136Xe at the tonne scale to determine whether the neutrino is its own antiparticle

summary.plain: A planned successor to EXO-200: a much bigger liquid-xenon detector, holding five tonnes of xenon, proposed for the SNOLAB underground laboratory in Canada. It would search for the same rare radioactive process, with far greater sensitivity.
summary.technical: nEXO: proposed tonne-scale (5 t, 136Xe enriched to ~90%) single-phase liquid-xenon TPC, successor to EXO-200, planned for SNOLAB (2 km depth). International consortium of >150 scientists from 31 institutions in 8 countries; as of 2026-10-25 the nEXO site (undated) still describes the experiment as under development, and no source consulted gives a construction start date.

unique_capabilities.quote: nEXO is a tonne-scale neutrinoless double beta (0νββ) decay search in 136Xe, based on the ultra-low background liquid xenon technology validated by EXO-200 ... As in EXO-200, the nEXO TPC is a LXe single-phase apparatus
unique_capabilities.value: Tonne-scale single-phase liquid-xenon TPC, scaling up the EXO-200 technique
